> > Vim's CI doesn't check leaks AFAIR.
> 
> Yes it does.

@chrisbra https://github.com/vim/vim/blob/master/.travis.yml does not have `ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=1` . So where is leak-detection enabled?

Based on http://releases.llvm.org/3.8.0/tools/clang/docs/AddressSanitizer.html#memory-leak-detection, clang 3.8+ (available on Ubuntu Xenial) enables it by default on Linux. Does `ASAN_OPTIONS` without `detect_leaks=1` override that behavior?
At the moment I am experiencing the crash quite often and was wondering as to what was the suggested option to workaround it?
@aignas if you build neovim from source, you can try https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/9921#issuecomment-484211699 and see if it helps.
If leak detection is on in CI, can a CI run determine if the line above is necessary?

Also, question from the core dump. What are these values supposed to have?

```
  ffs_fix_path = 0x9000000000000000 <no value available>
  ffs_wc_path = 0x00007f8c861c0004 "    endif"
```

Are they supposed to be paths? Why is `ffs_fix_path` a literal tab or is that just a coincidence and `0x9000000000000000` is not supposed to be a char?

> If leak detection is on in CI, can a CI run determine if the line above is necessary?

Send a PR and the CI will run.

> Also, question from the core dump. What are these values supposed to have?

If the pointers are garbage then the debugger will show garbage.

Actually don't bother, this should be fixed by vim-patch 8.1.0843 which I will merge now.
I wonder why Vim's CI which supposedly runs leak checks didn't catch this until Jan 2019...

            closes vim/vim#3877)
